§37.0561                                      §
                                              §




        TEXAS OIL & GAS ASSOCIATION COMMENTS TO PROPOSAL FOR
                    PUBLICATION OF NEW 16 TAC §25.194


The Texas Oil & Gas Association (TXOGA) appreciates the opportunity to provide comments on
proposed 16 Tex. Admin. Code (“TAC”) §25.194 to implement Public Utility Regulatory Act
(“PURA”) §37.0561, relating to Large Load Interconnection Standards. The Commission’s
proposal invites comments by April 17, 2025. As such these comments are timely filed.


TXOGA is a statewide trade association representing every facet of the Texas oil and gas industry
including small independents and major producers. Collectively, the membership of TXOGA
produces approximately 90 percent of Texas’ crude oil and natural gas, operates the vast majority
of the state’s refineries, LNG export capacity and pipelines, and includes a broad array of service
companies integral to the industry. In fiscal year 2025, the Texas oil and natural gas industry
supported over 495,000 direct jobs and paid $27 billion in state and local taxes and state royalties,
funding our state’s schools, roads and first responders.


As one of the most electricity-intensive industries in Texas, the oil and natural gas sector has a
vested interest in interconnection standards for large load customers. Senate Bill 6 states: “The
Commission by rule shall establish standards for interconnecting large load customers in the
ERCOT power region in a manner designed to support business development in this state while
minimizing the potential for stranded infrastructure costs and maintaining system reliability.” As
part of the mandate to support business development in this state, the Commission must consider
how these new requirements will affect development of traditional industrial facilities, including
oil and gas customer loads, in the ERCOT region.
 COMMENTS BY SECTION:


§25.194 (b) – Applicability
The applicability criteria in 25.194 (b) state that: “This section applies to a large load customer
that seeks…an expanded interconnection that equals or exceeds 75 MW for the first time…”.
TXOGA believes that imposing these interconnection requirements on legacy industrial facilities
that plan a small increase in peak demand such that their demand will transition from just below
75 MW to just above could present a disincentive to upgrading existing facilities and even
conducting routine facility maintenance. Imposing these interconnection requirements on a
facility that is increasing its demand by as little as a few megawatts also does not seem to be a
suitable use of limited ERCOT and utility staff resources.


TXOGA understands the desire to prevent new customers from avoiding these interconnection
requirements by requesting a 74 MW interconnection, and then quickly requesting to expand their
facility. But these requirements should not apply to facilities that were operating long before the
completion of SB6. One way to accommodate these legacy facilities would be to reword §25.194
(b) to read: “This section applies to a large load customer that seeks…(2) an expanded
interconnection for a facility that started operation after June 1, 2025, that equals or exceeds 75
MW for the first time…”.


§25.194 (d) (10) – Financial Security on a dollar per MW basis
TXOGA is concerned that the imposition of a financial security fee of $50,000/MW may represent
a persistent disincentive for industrial development in the state. Large industrial facilities often
require significant capital investment in long-lead time process equipment. This additional
financial cost to obtain electrical service could change the relative competitiveness of industrial
project development here in Texas compared to nearby states.


TXOGA would request that this fee be reduced to $20,000/MW, and that 50% of the fee be
refundable net any expenses incurred. To the extent this fee or a component thereof is specifically
intended to weed out speculative project development, TXOGA would reiterate that many large
oil and gas facilities require significant up-front capital investments, and these investments present
a strong indication that a project is moving forward.
 TXOGA would also ask that as part of this rulemaking process the Commission and the
transmission service providers provide more detail on how the interconnection fees collected from
new large load customers will be applied “…as an offset to the interconnecting TSPs rate base…”
as stated in 25.194 (f) (7) (b). How will these funds be applied so as to reduce TCOS for existing
customers?


§25.194 (e) – Interconnection study
As a point of clarification, section 25.194 (e) states that the interconnecting DSP or TSP must
coordinate with ERCOT to initiate the interconnection study within 60 days of executing the
intermediate agreement with the large load customer. Yet in Planning Guide Revision Request
(PGRR) 145, ERCOT seeks to replace individual interconnection studies with a batch study
process. Although the details of the batch process starting with Batch 1 are not yet known, it is
expected that these batches will be conducted every 6 or 12 months. It is not clear how the 60-day
deadline pairs with the expected frequency of future batch studies.


§25.194 (f) – Interconnection agreement
Section 25.194 (f) states that an interconnecting customer has 30 days following completion of the
interconnection study to execute an interconnection agreement with the interconnecting DSP and
TSP. If the customer fails to execute the agreement within that time, the interconnecting TSP must
cancel the interconnection request. This 30-day deadline may not provide sufficient time for an
industrial customer to receive all necessary internal approvals to allow execution of the
interconnection agreement contract. In particular, internal approval may require more time if the
interconnection study indicates that the customer will not receive the requested demand allocation
within the requested project development timeline. Results that have larger than anticipated
connection costs can also take longer to be approved. If the customer must consider the
implications of redesigning the project or accepting a delayed development timeline, that sort of
project viability analysis could take much longer than 30 days.


TXOGA requests that this 30-day deadline be extended to at least 90 days, or that there be some
accommodation in the rule for an extension of the deadline under situations where the customer
allocation is less than the amount requested. Additionally, TXOGA requests a requirement that
timeline and costs for the interconnection agreement be provided to the customer in a timely
manner.
 §25.194 (f) (7) – Non-refundable interconnection fee.
Similar to comments regarding Section 25.194 (d) (10), TXOGA would note that the non-
refundable payment of $50,000/MW due at the time the Interconnection Agreement is signed
in Section 25.194 (f) (7) in the staff proposal represents a significant additional project cost that
may alter investment decisions by large industrial customers.


§25.194 (g) – Withdrawal of all or a portion of requested peak demand or contracted peak
demand
Section 25.194 (g) states that only 20% of the balance of the financial security minus any
applicable interconnection expenses will be refunded to the customer in the event the customer
cancels the interconnection request. However, the proposal implies that this refund policy applies
even if the customer is denied all or most of its interconnection request through the proposed
ERCOT batch study process. Given the amount of development interest from large load customers
and the long-lead time for approval and construction of new transmission capacity, it is likely that
there will be many interconnecting projects that will not be allocated sufficient transmission
capacity to justify project development at least for several years into the future. In these situations,
if the customer decides to cancel the project, they should not be required to forfeit any of the
financial security beyond the actual costs incurred by the interconnecting TSP.




TXOGA appreciates the opportunity to comment and looks forward to continued engagement with
the Commission and stakeholders to implement SB6 in a manner that preserves reliability while
supporting Texas’ industrial competitiveness and economic growth.



Respectfully submitted,




Matt Patterson
Director of Government and Regulatory Affairs
Texas Oil & Gas Association

              TEXAS OIL & GAS ASSOCIATION EXECUTIVE SUMMARY



The Texas Oil & Gas Association (TXOGA) appreciates the opportunity to provide comments on
proposed 16 Tex. Admin. Code (“TAC”) §25.194 to implement Public Utility Regulatory Act
(“PURA”) §37.0561, relating to Large Load Interconnection Standards. As described in greater
detail in our comments we recommend:



•   Reword §25.194 (b) to read: “This section applies to a large load customer that seeks…(2) an
    expanded interconnection for a facility that started operation after June 1, 2025, that equals or
    exceeds 75 MW for the first time…”.

•   The financial security fee in §25.194 (d) (10) fee be reduced to $20,000/MW, and that 50% of
    the fee be refundable net any expenses incurred.

•   As part of this rulemaking process, the Commission and the transmission service providers
    provide more detail on how the interconnection fees collected from new large load customers
    will be applied “…as an offset to the interconnecting TSPs rate base…” as stated in 25.194 (f)
    (7) (b).

•   Clarification on how the 60-day interconnection study deadline in §25.194 (e) pairs with the
    expected frequency of future batch studies.

•   The 30-day interconnection agreement deadline in §25.194 (f) be extended to at least 90 days,
    or that there be some accommodation in the rule for an extension of the deadline under
    situations where the customer allocation is less than the amount requested, and a requirement
    that timeline and costs for the interconnection agreement be provided to the customer in a
    timely manner.

•   If the customer is denied all or most of its interconnection request, and if the customer decides
    to cancel a project (§25.194 (g)), the customer should not be required to forfeit any of the
    financial security beyond the actual costs incurred by the interconnecting TSP.
